questions.question: What is a simple event? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Definition A simple event is an event that contains only one sample point as its
  • elements – 2 marks. Example: When tossing a coin: getting head is a simple event,
  • getting tail is another simple event. When rolling a die: getting 3 is a simple event,
  • getting 6 is also a simple event. Symbolically: If the sample space S={1,2,3,4,5,6}
  • then E={3} is a simple event. – 1 mark
  • Or
  • Example alone – 2 marks
  • Maximum 3 marks

questions.question: Explain the various total and marginal concepts in economics with examples from cost, revenue, and utility analysis. Also show how marginal values are derived from total functions and why marginal concepts are critical for decision-making in economics? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Step 1: Meaning (2 marks)
  • • Total concepts measure the overall amount (e.g., Total Cost, Revenue, Utility).
  • • Marginal concepts measure the additional change in total when one more unit is
  • produced or consumed.
  • Step 2: Examples and Derivation (2 marks)
  • • Cost: MC = ΔTC/ΔQ → if TC rises from 500 to 520, MC = 20
  • • Revenue: MR = ΔTR/ΔQ → if TR rises from 1000 to 1070, MR = 70
  • • Utility: MU = ΔTU/ΔQ → if TU rises from 30 to 36, MU = 6
  • • In calculus: M=d(T)/dQ (e.g., if TC=100+5Q+Q2, then MC=5+2Q)
  • Step 3: Importance in Decision-Making (2 marks)
  • • Firms maximize profit where MC = MR.
  • • Consumers reach equilibrium where MU = Price.
  • • Marginal analysis guides optimal production, pricing, and resource use.
  • Total = 6 Marks (2 + 2 + 2)

questions.question: Write the formula for conditional probability when both A and B are dependent events. / [CO2]

  • formula: P(A∣B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) Alternatively, P(B∣A)=P(A∩B)/P(A)
  • Since A and B are dependent, we also know that:P(A∩B)=P(A∣B)⋅P(B)=P(B∣A)⋅P(A)
  • Hence, dependence means that P(A∣B)≠P(A) and P(B∣A)≠P(B).
  • Such proper explanation - 6 Marks
